IODream Vault CLI 0.4.1
Run apps with their secrets and keep secrets out of your code.

Usage
  iodreamvault <command> [options]   (IodreamVault and IODreamVault work too)

Commands
  login       Sign in through your browser
  logout      Forget the stored sign-in of the profile in use
  profile     List, switch, rename or remove saved sign-ins
  whoami      Show the server, profile, sign-in and your apps
  run         Run a command with secrets as environment variables
  export      Export secrets as .env, JSON or appsettings-style JSON
  pull        Print secrets as KEY=value lines or JSON
  get         Show a secret value, or a group as JSON
  list        List key names (values only with --values)
  set         Create or update a secret
  delete      Delete a key or a whole group
  use         Remember the app and environment for this folder
  scan        Find leaked secrets in code
  setup       Put iodreamvault on PATH for every shell
  update      Update to the latest version
  completion  Print the tab-completion script for a shell
  version     Show the version
  help        Show help

Global options
  --profile <name>   Saved sign-in to use (also IODREAMVAULT_PROFILE) (default: the folder's pinned profile, else the active one)
  --token <ivs_...>  ivs_ access token for CI. Discouraged: use IODREAMVAULT_TOKEN so it stays out of shell history
  --verbose          Show the server and how you're signed in (also -v)
  --no-color         Plain output without colours (also NO_COLOR=1)
  --no-update-check  Don't check for a newer version (also IODREAMVAULT_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1)
  --help             Show help for a command (also -h)

Environment
  IODREAMVAULT_TOKEN            An ivs_ access token for CI: no browser, wins over profiles
  IODREAMVAULT_SERVER           Vault address for the token (default https://vault.iodream.co.uk)
  IODREAMVAULT_PROFILE          Saved sign-in to use (like --profile)
  NO_COLOR                      Turn colours off

Examples
  $ iodreamvault login
  $ iodreamvault run --app MyApp --
[truncated]

iodreamvault login — Sign in through your browser

Uses the same sign-in as the AI plugin. Each profile keeps its own sign-in (server, company, token) in the macOS Keychain, Windows DPAPI or ~/.config/iodreamvault (600). Without --profile it signs in to the profile in use (default: 'default').

Usage
  iodreamvault login [--profile <name>] [options]

Options
  --server <url>  Vault address (default: the signed-in server, or IODREAMVAULT_SERVER, or https://vault.iodream.co.uk)
  --no-browser    Don't open a browser: print the address (for SSH and headless machines)

Examples
  $ iodreamvault login
  $ iodreamvault login --profile work --server https://vault.example.com
  $ iodreamvault login --no-browser

Global options: --profile, --token, --verbose, --no-color, --no-update-check, --help

result.stdout:
iodreamvault run — Run a command with secrets as environment variables

Section:Key becomes Section__Key, which .NET configuration reads. Values are never printed or written to disk. If approval is needed, the link is shown and the CLI waits.
iv:// references: any environment variable or --env-file value like iv://Key (the folder's app and environment) or iv://App/Env/Key (spaces or %20 both work; leave a part empty for the default, e.g. iv:///Dev/Key) is replaced by the vault value before the command starts; a group becomes JSON. If one can't be resolved, all problems are listed and nothing starts. A variable set in your shell wins over the file.

Usage
  iodreamvault run --app <name> --env <name> [options] -- <command...>

Options
  --app <name>        App name (needed when you can use several apps)
  --env <name>        Environment, for example Dev, Staging or Prod (default: Prod)
  --path <Group:Sub>  Only keys under this group, for example Authentication:Google (default: everything)
  --env-file <file>   Load KEY=value lines from this file; iv:// references in it are filled in
  --server <url>      Vault address (default: the signed-in server, or IODREAMVAULT_SERVER, or https://vault.iodream.co.uk)

Examples
  $ iodreamvault run --app MyApp --env Dev -- dotnet run
  $ iodreamvault run --app "My App" --env Prod --path Authentication -- npm start
  $ iodreamvault run --env-file .env -- npm start

Global options: --profile, --token, --verbose, --no-color, --no-update-check, --help

iodreamvault export — Export secrets as .env, JSON or appsettings-style JSON

Prints to the screen unless you give -o. Uses the folder defaults from iodreamvault use; your permissions and approvals apply.

Usage
  iodreamvault export [--app <name>] [--env <name>] [options]

Options
  --app <name>                     App name (needed when you can use several apps)
  --env <name>                     Environment, for example Dev, Staging or Prod (default: Prod)
  --path <Group:Sub>               Only keys under this group, for example Authentication:Google (default: everything)
  --format <env|json|dotnet-json>  env (KEY__SUB=value), json (flat Section:Key) or dotnet-json (nested, like appsettings.json) (default: env)
  --output <file>                  Write to this file instead of the screen (permissions 600; also -o). Warns if git could commit it
  --env-file <file>                Export only this file, with its iv:// references filled in (e.g. .env.template)
  --server <url>                   Vault address (default: the signed-in server, or IODREAMVAULT_SERVER, or https://vault.iodream.co.uk)

Examples
  $ iodreamvault export
  $ iodreamvault export --format dotnet-json -o appsettings.Local.json
  $ iodreamvault export --app MyApp --env Dev --format json
  $ iodreamvault export --env-file .env.template -o .env

Global options: --profile, --token, --verbose, --no-color, --no-update-check, --help

result.stdout:
iodreamvault scan — Find leaked secrets in code

Respects .gitignore and skips bin, obj, node_modules, .git and binary files. Mark false alarms with an iodreamvault:ignore comment or a .iodreamvaultignore entry. Exits with 1 when something is found. The hook follows core.hooksPath and husky (.husky/pre-commit), appends to an existing hook, and works in Git Bash on Windows. Skip it once with git commit --no-verify. --vault needs a sign-in (or IODREAMVAULT_TOKEN) with the right to read values; signed-in accounts approve it like a read.

Usage
  iodreamvault scan [path] [options]

Options
  --staged           Only the lines staged for the next git commit
  --install-hook     Add a git pre-commit hook that runs scan --staged and blocks commits with findings
  --uninstall-hook   Remove that hook (other hook lines are kept)
  --history          Scan every commit in the git history (git log -p --all): shows commit, file and line
  --since <date>     With --history: only commits after this date
  --max-commits <n>  With --history: only the newest N commits
  --vault            Also flag values stored in the vault. Only key names and salted hashes are fetched; values never leave the vault
  --app <name>       App name (needed when you can use several apps)
  --env <name>       Environment, for example Dev, Staging or Prod (default: Prod)
  --server <url>     Vault address (default: the signed-in server, or IODREAMVAULT_SERVER, or https://vault.iodream.co.uk)

Examples
  $ iodreamvault scan
  $ iodreamvault scan src/
  $ iodreamvault scan --staged
  $ iodreamvault scan --install-hook
  $ iodreamvault scan --history --since 2026-01-01
  $ iodreamvault scan --vault
  $ iodreamvault scan --history --vault --app "My App" --env Prod

Global options: --profile, --token, --verbose, --no-color, --no-update-check, --help

iodreamvault setup — Put iodreamvault on PATH for every shell

zsh, bash, sh and fish on macOS/Linux (profile files), the user PATH on Windows. Also adds the IodreamVault and IODreamVault names on Unix.

Usage
  iodreamvault setup [options]

Options
  --check         Only report; exit 1 if something is missing
  --dir <folder>  Folder to add instead of this program's folder

Examples
